title: The WORST muscle building advice (Functional bros MUST be stopped)
summary: NH attacks the reverse-engineering advice to replicate an athlete's performance to get their muscles, such as using gymnastic rings for gymnast biceps. Such byproducts take thousands of hours, the approach has a terrible time-to-stimulus ratio, and bodybuilders, as anti-specialists, should use lifts built for hypertrophy like curls.
claims: The worst muscle-building advice is to build a muscle by replicating the performance of someone who has it, which assumes strength equals size
Strength standards come from the same flawed logic, e.g. 'get a 200 lb overhead press and you'll have big shoulders'
'Train like an athlete' is meaningless: athletes are defined by skills, not looks, and come in every shape
Using gymnastic rings to build gymnast biceps fails because gymnasts get them as a byproduct of 10+ years of 5-6 hours of daily training
Training rings for biceps is like becoming a chess grandmaster to improve your memory
Perhaps 0.1% of lifters have progressively overloaded their arms for 10+ years; most never train arms consistently
Ring proponents also claim curls don't work, steering people away from a valid method
Time-to-stimulus ratio matters as much as fatigue-to-stimulus; choose exercises that give the most results for the least time
Curls beat rings on time-to-stimulus because they need no learning; you'd get similar results in a tenth of the time
By the same logic you'd become a pro cyclist for quads, a swimmer for shoulders and a ballerina for calves
Real strength athletes and gymnasts never give this advice; it usually comes from men in their 30s-40s on TRT who rediscovered fitness
Go to the source: a gymnast for rings, a powerlifter for the bench, a bodybuilder for bigger biceps
Resistance training was created by isolating the resistance part of functional farm labor to maximize muscle; going back is regression
Bodybuilding is using any means necessary to grow; the bodybuilder is an anti-specialist and anti-technique, and hypertrophy is itself a function
Bodybuilders are artists, not athletes: they borrow from sports, take only what's needed and reduce it to the minimum
NH uses some ring movements in his own training but will never become a gymnast
Some pursuit of strength is needed because muscles grow as demands increase (progressive overload), but chasing performance makes you a strength coper with a bad physique
exercises: designed for biceps growth; best time-to-stimulus
huge skill investment; poor time-to-stimulus for biceps
